reason: The core mechanism is contradicted by this poller's own history. PC32-05 claims time.sleep(600) does not count standby, so the first header after a wake lags by ~10-13 min. On 28 Sep the same lb_poll.py (Python 3.12.10) wrote a header at 14:54:21Z. Modern Standby began at 15:00Z with ~4.5 min of the sleep left. The next loop iteration started at 15:15:31Z (poll.log l.23505, DNS NameResolutionError notes), the exact second of the brief battery-budget wake (CONTEXT l.4000-4001: 18:15:31 MSK). If standby were not counted, the poll would have run ~15:20Z. So the sleep counted standby and fired at the wake. The 15:41:53Z header comes from a restarted process (CONTEXT l.3982-3983), so it proves nothing either way. The failure mode actually seen is a DNS failure just after the wake followed by hung loops (CONTEXT l.4070). The existing post-wake step already covers it (G1 '< 15 min' header, 'restart any stale loop', N.4 75/100-min limits, W6 one-instance rule at CONTEXT l.2064). The 'confirm exactly one of each' step is already true: at 03:3xZ Win32_Process shows exactly one lb_poll.py (37016), one e10_watch_loop.py (18040 under 19596) and one run_feed_loop.sh (10924). There is only one real lag source, and it is not the one claimed: the header timestamp is taken before poll() (l.25), but the header is written only after up to 3 x (180 s timeout + 30 s sleep), about 630 s. The first night reads are ~07:05Z, so an 11-min lag at 06:07Z changes no decision. No score value; it is ops text only.
fix: Do not adopt the 'standby not counted, pre-sleep header expected' premise or the fixed 13-min wait. At 06:07Z: (1) read the wake time from the Kernel-Power events. (2) The poller is healthy if the newest header's timestamp is >= the wake time. The poller is alive and possibly still inside poll() if the newest header predates the wake but lb_poll.py is alive and less than ~11 min (630 s, the poll() retry bound) have passed since the wake: re-check once at wake + 11 min, then kill and restart that one PID. Restart right away if no lb_poll.py process is alive. (3) Keep N.4's 75/100-min limits for the e10 and feed loops, and the W6 one-instance check (it holds now: 37016 / 18040 / 10924). No change to lb_poll.py.
realistic_gain: None on the LB or private score. At most, one needless poller restart (one extra Kaggle call) is avoided if the check happens to fall inside the ~11-min poll() retry window after the wake. The first read that matters is ~07:05Z, well after it.
